name: Furniture rental (category guide)
summary: Rent vs buy for bare/semi-furnished condos — short EP tours, humidity-aware pieces, and exit disposal so orphan sofas do not eat the security deposit.
body: Singapore ‘unfurnished’ often means washer + fridge + blinds, not beds — decode the inventory annex before you budget CapEx. Furniture rental (monthly packages, sofa/bed/desk bundles) wins on 6–18 month EP tours and diplomatic exits when buying and dumping would cost more than rent. Buy (IKEA / Carousell / mid-tier) wins on 2+ year stays if you accept humidity (dehumidifier ROI) and a planned exit sale or paid disposal. Never assume the landlord will buy your pieces at the end — forum threads treat that as a bonus, not a right. Check who owns damage liability under the rental contract, delivery/lift booking fees, and whether packages include mattresses that survive tropical mould. Pair rental quotes against self-storage for between-lease holds and local movers for lift deposits. This is a category guide to the rent-vs-buy decision, not a ranked furniture-brand list. Family ops note: chickenpox / recovery weeks punish households that still lack a washable spare duvet and blackout for daytime naps — rent or buy the boring kit before the next exclusion letter. Family ops: drama-studio waiting rooms are a weekly belonging rail — put the class window on the shared calendar before you restack the living room for guests.
whenToEngage: Bare / semi-furnished unit and stay under ~18 months
Need beds night-one without full CapEx
Diplomatic clause / early exit makes buy-and-dump painful
Comparing rental packages vs Carousell + disposal fees
